titre: Preah Vihear (1962): A Map Left Unanswered Becomes a Border
accroche: In 1962, the Hague Court awards a temple to Cambodia on the strength of a 1907 map that Thailand had left unanswered for half a century.
contenu_vulgarise:
The Preah Vihear temple stands on the edge of a cliff in the Dangrek range, on the border between Cambodia and Thailand. In 1954, Thai forces move in. On October 6, 1959, Cambodia brings the case to the International Court of Justice. On June 15, 1962, the Court rules in its favor by nine votes to three. Yet it does not decide whether the line on the map follows the watershed.

## A Treaty That Says One Thing, a Map That Says Another

The Franco-Siamese treaty of February 13, 1904 fixes the border in this sector along the watershed line, and provides for a mixed commission to mark it on the ground. The maps are finally drawn up by French officers, completed in the fall of 1907 and handed to the Siamese government in 1908. One of them, which the case file calls Annex I, places the temple on the Cambodian side. But the line on this map does not follow the watershed everywhere: a survey of 1934–1935 finds the discrepancy.

Thailand therefore argues three things. The map has no binding character. Its line is not the true watershed line. And if it ever accepted it, it was under the mistaken belief that it followed that line. The Court does not examine which of these arguments is right on the ground. It looks at what Thailand did, or did not do, with the map.

## Fifty Years of Silence

It notes that Thailand did not raise the question of the map before the 1958 negotiations. In 1930, Prince Damrong visits the temple, and the French Resident of the neighboring Cambodian province receives him officially on the spot: Siam does not protest. During the negotiations of 1925, 1937 and 1947, natural occasions to raise the question, Thailand again says nothing. For about fifty years, it also drew benefit from the advantages the 1904 treaty gave it. The Court adds that authorities who accepted the map without examining it can no longer plead error to vitiate their consent. A few local acts of the Thai administration carry no weight against the consistent attitude of the central authorities.

It concludes that Thailand accepted the map, and that the line drawn on it became, for both States, the treaty border. There is then no need to check whether that line follows the watershed. The operative part requires Thailand to withdraw its forces from the temple and, by seven votes to five, to return to Cambodia the objects removed since 1954.

## The Shift

It is often said that the Court confirmed the treaty line. It did almost the opposite: it set aside what the treaty said about the watershed, because the conduct of the States had replaced it with the map. A State's silence before a document that binds it can amount to consent. In 2013, seized again by Cambodia after clashes, the Court clarified that its 1962 judgment covered the promontory of the temple, but not all the neighboring heights, such as Phnom Trap.

repere.texte: On June 15, 1962, the International Court of Justice rules, by nine votes to three, that the Temple of Preah Vihear is situated in Cambodian territory. It does not examine whether the line of the 1907 map follows the watershed line.
repere.source: International Court of Justice, Temple of Preah Vihear (Cambodia v. Thailand), summary of the judgment of June 15, 1962

carte.punch: In 1962, a temple changes countries on the strength of a map Bangkok had not contested before 1958.
carte.idee: The 1904 treaty set the border along the watershed; the 1907 map did not follow it everywhere. Since Thailand did not react for about fifty years, the Court rules in 1962 that the map governs and that it need not check the line.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Request for interpretation of the judgment of June 15, 1962 (International Court of Justice, case no. 151)
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The page of the proceedings opened by Cambodia in 2011, with the judgment of November 11, 2013.

quiz.question: Why does the Court consider it unnecessary to check whether the line on the map actually follows the watershed?
choix: Because the mixed commission had approved the map in 1907 as exactly reproducing the watershed line
Because Thailand had accepted the map through its silence and conduct, and could no longer plead error
Because the 1904 treaty made no reference to the watershed line
Because an arbitral award of 1904 had already fixed the watershed line
quiz.explication: The 1904 treaty does refer to the watershed line, and the Court does not say that the map reproduced it, leaving the question open. The 1904 treaty provides for a mixed commission, not an arbitration. What decides the case is Thailand's acceptance of the map: it did not contest it for about fifty years and can no longer invoke error.

quiz_supplementaire.question: When Cambodia returns to the Court in 2013, what does the interpretation judgment clarify about the scope of the 1962 judgment?
choix: It confirms sovereignty over the temple promontory only, not the neighboring heights
It extends Cambodian sovereignty to the whole Dangrek range
It annuls the 1962 judgment and orders a new border demarcation
It entrusts management of the temple to a joint administration of the two countries
quiz_supplementaire.explication: In 2013, the Court clarifies that its 1962 judgment covered only the temple promontory, and not all the neighboring heights such as Phnom Trap, the object of the more recent clashes.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What happens when Prince Damrong visits the temple in 1930?
choix: Siamese authorities bar him from the temple, which they consider their territory
The French Resident of the neighboring Cambodian province receives him officially on the spot, with no Siamese protest
He publicly protests the French presence at the site
He signs, on behalf of Siam, an agreement recognizing the 1907 map
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Prince Damrong is officially received by the French Resident without Siam protesting, an episode the Court counts among the signs of Thai silence over fifty years.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who draws the border maps provided for by the 1904 Franco-Siamese treaty, and when are they handed to the Siamese government?
choix: A neutral Swiss commission, which hands them to both governments in 1910
Siamese officers, who send them to France for validation in 1907
French officers, who complete the maps in the fall of 1907 and hand them to Siam in 1908
The International Court of Justice itself, during the 1959 proceedings
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The mixed commission provided for by the 1904 treaty entrusts the drawing to French officers; the maps, completed in the fall of 1907, are handed to the Siamese government in 1908.
